text:
alex: Heads up — we're seeing a provisioning slowdown in us-west1. Several GPU hosts stuck in PROVISIONING for >3m. Logs point at local SSD write queues backing up.

rachel: hitting the same for a handful of pods. Any iostat or dmesg yet?

alex: pasted a quick iostat from one impacted host:
```
Device            tps    rkB/s    wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm %util
nvme0n1         512.00     32.0   8192.0   33.0    60.12 120.00  0.20 119.80  2.50 128.00
```

cheng: whoa, avgqu-sz 60 and %util >100-ish on the metric means heavy queueing. Could be high GC/scrub activity + batch checkpoints.

alex: dmesg snippet shows repeated cleanup daemon writes and some SMART errors: 
```
[12345.678] scrubber[2048]: trimming 8G bucket id=0x3a
[12346.001] nvme0: SMART warning: 0x02 media_wearout_indicator=93
[12346.005] nvme0: write error -22 at sector 0x1f4b00
```

ops-oncall: alert: gpu-provisioner delayed 14 hosts in us-west1, rolling fallback to smaller instance type in progress. :warning:

rachel: Is this the janitor/scrub overlap we saw last month? If cleaners and large checkpoint flushes collide with provisioning we get write amplification.

cheng: exactly. Two levers: pause background scrubs on hosts with active provisioning, and apply io-weight caps to janitor processes. We should also avoid full-drain/evict cycles during peak provisioning windows.

alex: quick mitigation plan: 1) set scrub throttle to 30% for us-west1 with feature flag, 2) add --io-weight=10 to janitor on GPU pools, 3) enable immediate fencing fallback to shared pool where possible.

rachel: agree. Also let's add a short-term quota on large checkpoint jobs from training tenants — they were spiking writes. Can we identify top writers?

alex: running a quick blktrace to correlate — will post results in 10m. For now I've paused aggressive scrub on 6 hosts (manual) and bumped provisioning fallback threshold to 70% to allow API to route to spare capacity.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: scrub-throttle feature-flag toggled for us-west1 by alex at 2987654500.

cheng: if SMART shows wearout >=90 we should avoid heavy rewrites. For hosts with media_wearout_indicator >=90, mark for replacement after graceful drain. We should avoid using them for provisioning-heavy tasks.

ops-oncall: cost note — replacing drives early increases capex but reduces incident risk. Recommend we surface a short cost/ops tradeoff to infra-leads.

rachel: agreed, create a small PRD. Meanwhile, alex — can you post blktrace snippet and a list of top 5 writer pods? I want to notify tenant owners.

alex: posting summary: top writers are training-batch-42, checkpoint-worker-7, metrics-aggregator-3. Blktrace shows long bursts (200MB/s) from checkpoint-worker after snapshot merges.

cheng: temporary throttle policy: 1) cap pod write bandwidth to 80MB/s for checkpoint jobs during provisioning windows, 2) prefer remote NFS for large model checkpoints in us-west1, 3) classify hosts with wear>=90 as degraded and route flows away.

rachel: I'll own tenant comms. ops-oncall, can you put this in the incident board and add cost estimate for 10 drive replacements?

ops-oncall: done — incident 2026-IR-782 created. Assigned to infra-leads for replacement approval.

alex: follow-ups: schedule rolling replacement for 6 high-wear nvmes next weekend; rollout scrub-throttle cluster-wide if stable; implement automatic scrub backoff during provisioning in the agent code (tracking ticket infra/433).

cheng: thanks — also let's add a metric alarm for avgqu-sz >20 on nvme devices per host (US regions) so we catch earlier.

rachel: noted. if anything changes ping #eng-infra. :thumbsup:
